confidence.label: Confidence
confidence.plain: How sure the model is about this forecast, based on how much history and match data it had.

shift.label: Division adjustment
shift.plain: Suggested change to a player's division for the next tournament (＋ moves up, − moves down).

impact.label: Impact
impact.plain: How much better or worse the player did than expected for the match-up — 0–100 within their role.

vs_local.label: vs similar players
vs_local.plain: Performance compared to players of the same role and nearby division (0 = average, ＋ above, − below).

points.label: Move signal

recent_moves.label: Recent moves
recent_moves.plain: Division changes in the player's last two tournaments.

forecast_place.label: Forecast place
forecast_place.plain: Where the model expects the team to finish.

likely_range.label: Likely finish
likely_range.plain: Where the team lands in 80% of simulated tournaments (10th–90th percentile).

prob_top.label: Chance for top finish
prob_top.plain: Share of simulated tournaments where the team finished in the top N.

competitiveness.label: How close
competitiveness.plain: How back-and-forth the match was — 100 is a nail-biter, 0 is a blowout.

predictability.label: How expected
predictability.plain: How well the result matched the pre-match forecast — 100 means it went as expected.

skill_balance.label: How even
skill_balance.plain: How evenly matched the two teams' ratings were — 100 is a perfectly even match-up.

match_quality.label: Match quality
match_quality.plain: Overall watchability: a blend of how close, how expected and how even the match was.

forecast_miss.label: Forecast miss
forecast_miss.plain: How far the forecast landed from the real finish, in places.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.plain: Weighted amount of history behind the forecast — more evidence means more confidence.

newcomer.label: Newcomer
newcomer.plain: Playing their first tournament, or their first time in this role.

why_score.label: Why this score
why_score.plain: The player stats that pushed the impact score up or down the most.

smurf.label: Possible smurf
smurf.plain: Playing well above their division — could be a strong player on an under-ranked account.

throw.label: Possible throw
throw.plain: Looks like they stopped trying mid-series — play dropped sharply below their own usual level.

troll.label: Possible griefing
troll.plain: Repeatedly playing below their own level, dragging their team down.

sandbag.label: Possible sandbag
sandbag.plain: One unexpectedly weak tournament that stands out against the player's own track record.

climbing.label: Climbing
climbing.plain: Players the model thinks are playing above their division and should move up a tier.

dropping.label: Dropping
dropping.plain: Players performing below their division — the model leans toward moving them down a tier.

watch.label: Watch flags
watch.plain: Automatic heads-ups when someone's results look unusual. A prompt for a human to look — never a verdict.

avg_confidence.label: Average confidence
avg_confidence.plain: How much data is behind the calls across the whole bracket. It climbs as more maps are played.

upsets.label: Upsets
upsets.plain: Teams that finished four or more places away from their predicted spot — the bracket's biggest surprises.

new_faces.label: New faces
new_faces.plain: Players new to the tournament, or playing a role they haven't before. Their numbers carry less weight until we see more.

predicted_move.label: Predicted move
predicted_move.plain: Whether the model thinks a player belongs in a higher (climb) or lower (drop) division than they're in now. Hold means they're right where they should be.

impact_percentile.label: Impact percentile
impact_percentile.plain: Where a player's impact ranks among others in the same role and division — 90 means they beat almost everyone at their level.

terms.intro: These Terms of Service ("Terms") govern your access to and use of {siteName}. By creating an account or using the site, you agree to these Terms.

acceptance.title: Acceptance of these Terms
acceptance.body: By signing in or otherwise using {siteName}, you agree to be bound by these Terms and by our Privacy Policy. If you don't agree, don't use the site.

service.title: About the service
service.body: {siteName} is a fan-run platform for organizing and tracking esports tournaments: brackets, match reporting, drafts, and player statistics. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by any game publisher or developer.

eligibility.title: Eligibility
eligibility.body: You must be at least 13 years old to use {siteName}, and old enough to hold an account with whichever OAuth provider you sign in with. If local law sets a higher minimum age for online services, that age applies instead.

accounts.title: Accounts and sign-in
accounts.body: There is no separate password: you sign in through Discord, Twitch, or Battle.net OAuth, and {siteName} stores the profile information that provider returns (username, avatar, and a stable identifier) together with any tournament data tied to your account. You're responsible for keeping that OAuth account secure — anyone who can sign in to it can sign in as you here.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.body: Some communities run their own branded workspace on {siteName} — a self-contained set of tournaments, teams, and stats with its own administrators. Workspace administrators can see the membership, roles, and tournament activity within their own workspace only. Any signed-in account can create a workspace and becomes its owner; new workspaces are listed publicly only after the platform team reviews them.

conduct.title: Tournament conduct
conduct.body: When you register for or play in a tournament, you agree to report match results accurately, follow that tournament's rules, and accept the ruling of its organizers on disputes. Falsifying a match report, colluding on results, or evading a suspension by registering under another identity is a breach of these Terms.

content.title: Your content
content.body: Anything you submit — match reports, screenshots, logs, an avatar, a workspace's branding — stays yours, but you grant {siteName} a license to store, display, and process it for the purpose of running the tournaments and stats you submitted it for. Don't upload anything you don't have the right to share.

prohibited.title: Prohibited conduct
prohibited.body: Don't attempt to bypass access controls, scrape or overload the API outside documented use, impersonate another player or organizer, or use the platform to harass other users. We may remove content, void tournament results, or suspend an account that violates this section.

suspension.title: Suspension and termination
suspension.body: We can suspend or terminate access for violating these Terms, at a platform level or, for workspace-specific misconduct, at a workspace level by that workspace's administrators. You can stop using the service at any time; ask a platform administrator to close your account and its associated data.

thirdParty.title: Third-party services

privacy.metaDescription: How {siteName} collects, uses, and protects your data.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains what {siteName} collects when you use the site, why, and who can see it. It covers the platform itself; each workspace sets its own community rules separately.

collection.title: Information we collect
collection.body: When you sign in, your OAuth provider (Discord, Twitch, or Battle.net) gives us a stable account identifier, your username or display name, and your avatar; some providers also share an email address. As you use the site we also store what you generate directly: tournament registrations, match and map reports, draft picks, and any roles assigned to you. Standard web infrastructure logs (IP address, user agent) are kept briefly for security and abuse prevention.

use.title: How we use it
use.body: We use this information to run tournaments and drafts, attribute match results and statistics to the right player, enforce the roles and permissions you've been granted, and keep the site secure. We don't use it for advertising, and we don't sell it.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: {siteName} sets a session cookie to keep you signed in, a cookie recording your active workspace so a custom-domain workspace shows the right branding, a locale cookie for your language preference, and a time-zone cookie so dates show in your local time. These functional cookies are required for the site to work. Google Analytics and Yandex Metrica cookies, which measure how pages are used, are optional: they load only after you accept them in the cookie notice, and declining keeps them off. You can change that choice at any time from "Cookie settings" in the site footer; withdrawing it also deletes the analytics cookies already stored. No advertising cookies are set.

sharing.title: Who can see your information
sharing.body: Your public profile (name, avatar, tournament history, and stats) is visible to anyone who can view the workspace it belongs to. Workspace administrators can see the membership and roles within their own workspace. We share account data with OAuth providers only to the extent needed to authenticate you, and we don't otherwise share it with third parties.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: Account and tournament data is kept for as long as your account exists, since match history and statistics remain part of the historical record of a tournament even after it ends. Infrastructure logs are rotated on a much shorter schedule.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can review the profile information tied to your account from your account settings. To request a correction or deletion of your account and its data, contact a platform administrator through the project's GitHub repository; deleting an account may anonymize rather than remove historical match records where full removal would corrupt another player's tournament history.

children.title: Children's privacy
children.body: {siteName} is not directed at children under 13, and we don't knowingly collect data from them beyond what their OAuth provider already restricts by its own age requirements.

security.title: Security
security.body: We rely on your OAuth provider for authentication rather than storing a password ourselves, and access to administrative data is restricted by the same role-based permissions that govern the rest of the platform. No online service can guarantee absolute security.

changes.title: Changes to this Policy
changes.body: We may update this Privacy Policy as the platform changes. Continuing to use {siteName} after a change takes effect means you accept the revised Policy.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions about this Privacy Policy can be filed as an issue on the project's GitHub repository.
